raw_response:
I farm 8 mu here in Quzhou, wheat and maize like everyone around me. My father farmed this land, now I farm it. I've been doing this 25 years so I know what works.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed from the dealer in town — Jimai variety, what most neighbors plant. Works fine here. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before sowing, that's about 50 kg. Then in spring when wheat greens up, I topdress with urea, maybe one bag per mu — 40 kg or so. That gives me around 28 kg N total, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu. Less and the wheat looks yellow, more is wasting money. I water 3 times usually — before winter, at greening, and at filling if no rain. Spray for aphids and powdery mildew, 2 times. Harvest around 450-500 kg/mu if weather is normal.

For maize, plant right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar — everyone uses hybrid now, the old seed gives nothing. One bag compound fertilizer at sowing plus urea at big trumpet stage, one bag. That's about 22 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K. Maize needs less than wheat I find. Water once or twice if July is dry, my well is fine. Spray for borer and armyworm, 2 times. I get about 550 kg/mu normal years.

I use rotary tiller — village has one for rent, cheap. No one ploughs deep anymore. My wife helps at harvest, sons work in town but come back for busy times.
